mathematics.assertion_tested: Independent exact coefficient routes, quartic packet reconstruction, residual squaring, Euler polynomial identities, finite-difference kernels and prime residual controls agree in the enumerated finite ranges.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: Z and Q, exact Python integers and fractions; polynomial and truncated formal-series coefficient arrays
mathematics.conventions: s_n is the positive coefficient of t^(2n)/(2n)! in sec(t); a_n=(-1)^n*s_n is the signed Euler number E_(2n). P_N,n(r) uses t^(N*n)/(N*n)!, not t^n/n!. All coefficient arrays are in ascending ordinary power order.
inputs: N=2..6, n=0..10, r=-2,-1,0,1/2,1,2,3; N=1 is a separate boundary control
All coefficients of the bivariate addition identity for N=2..6 and n=0..8
OEIS A000364 indices 0..15 and A211212 indices 0..11, explicitly embedded and attributed
Rank dynamic programming for N=2..6 and block count 0..8; explicit permutations at (N,length)=(2,0),(2,4),(2,6),(2,8),(4,4),(4,8)
Quartic-to-secant indices n=0..40; two packet coefficients at u^0..u^11
Newton residuals modulo t^32, iterations 0..4; Euler polynomials of degree 0..12
Three explicitly generated integer sequences, M=1..5, every 0<=s<M and difference order 0..5
Refinement composition M,L=1..4, all admitted offsets, and order 0..3
Prime residual polynomials for p=2,3,5,7,11 and their application to the three sequences
non_claims: Finite checks do not prove the universal identities; written proofs are reviewed separately.
